start_here: Say to your AI: "Make a word template from bakery/transcript.json, where Sam says: Sam baked 40 loaves before dawn and sold them all." It runs tool:make-a-word-template and writes bakery/TEMPLATE.json.

lists.label: Settings
lists.holds: One row per tool and scope (a person, a film, a piece or the whole account): the settings that tool reads when it runs, as JSON. For this folder the account row holds your own dimensions registry.
alike: a config sheet or settings spreadsheet
a notes page of defaults per project

instructions: 1. Get a word-timed transcript of your piece (a JSON file {"words":[{"text","start","end"}]}), or write a spec, or point at a post, caption file or folder of images. Put it in your scratch folder, for example bakery/transcript.json.

2. Say to your AI: "Make a word template from bakery/transcript.json". It reads the row with tools:list {tool: "tool:make-a-word-template"} and runs its command from the root of the Workshop checkout: python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/make_template.py bakery/transcript.json bakery/TEMPLATE.json

3. Read the one summary line and open bakery/TEMPLATE.md beside the output: which words are fixed (KEEP), each slot with its rule (here the number 40 is slot auto-number-w2 by rule R1-number), and every dimension still pending with why.
4. If it exits 2, read standard error: it says what to change in the input.
5. Next fill the slot with tool:fill-a-word-template, and judge any rewrite with tool:check-words-against-a-word-template.
6. Optional: if you keep your own dimensions registry as a row of list:settings, read that row with records:read, write it to a file and add --settings-record FILE to the command.

worked_examples.title: A spoken line becomes a template with one number slot
worked_examples.ask: Make a word template from bakery/transcript.json.
worked_examples.given: Read from tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/make_template.py and run for real on a made-up transcript (11 timed words: "Sam baked 40 loaves before dawn and sold them all."): python3 -I tools/fill-a-template-without-changing-its-words/do-work/make_template.py bakery/transcript.json bakery/TEMPLATE.json
worked_examples.hands_back: Exit 0 and the line: bakery/TEMPLATE.json: 11 tokens (1 SLOT in 1 slots), 4 dimensions measured, 14 pending; view bakery/TEMPLATE.md. The slot is auto-number-w2, type NUMBER, rule R1-number, value 40; the other 9 words are KEEP.

pour.how: Name the list you already keep for tool settings and read it with records:read (its fields and row type). Run tool:pour-example-rows-into-my-list with that list as into and list:settings as kit_list: it matches each kit field to one of yours (your map, the same id, the same label, or a name in alike), pours nothing under 80% and names the fields with no home, and otherwise answers the one records:write that adds the example rows beside your own.
